title: ynotes --json output
description: The machine-facing contract for every `ynotes <cmd> --json` output (`save`, `query`, `list`, `show`, `update`, `delete`, `prune`, `reanchor`, `reindex`, `doctor`, `lookup`). `query --count` and `list --count` emit a condensed status-breakdown payload instead of the notes (see queryCountData / listCountData). Every shape rides inside the same envelope: `{success: bool, v: int, …}` — `data` on success, `error`+`type` on failure. The envelope is emitted on stdout regardless of exit code, so a JSON consumer never has to branch on `$?` to parse the response. This is a stable, versioned agent contract: `v` is bumped whenever a field changes and mirrored in tests/agent_contract.rs. See AGENTS.md invariant 7.

successEnvelope.title: success envelope
successEnvelope.description: Carries a successful result. Emitted on a `0` exit by every command, and also by `delete` on a `1` exit when some requested ids were unresolved (see `deleteData`) — so a success envelope does not by itself imply a `0` exit. The `data` shape depends on the subcommand; the envelope fields are uniform across all of them.

failureEnvelope.title: failure envelope
failureEnvelope.description: Emitted when the command itself failed: exit `2` for a usage error, exit `1` for an engine/io/render failure. The converse does not hold — a non-zero exit is not always a failure envelope: `delete` reports unresolved ids inside a *success* envelope and still exits `1` (see `deleteData`). The diagnostic that would otherwise go to stderr is in-band as `error`; `type` is a stable enum so a consumer can branch programmatically without regex on the message.

error.description: The diagnostic message — the same text that would otherwise appear on stderr.

type.description: Error class. `usage`: bad invocation / bad value (exit 2). `engine`: an engine-level failure (exit 1). `io`: a binary-side I/O failure (exit 1). `render`: serialisation failure (exit 1).

saveData.title: save --json data
saveData.description: Payload for `ynotes save --json`: the saved note's identity. The id is a content hash of (target, scope, anchor, body) with no timestamp, so it is deterministic across machines and a retried identical save is a no-op. Note: a subsequent `reanchor` (or `update`) changes the anchor and therefore the id — use (target, scope, body) as the stable lineage when caching a reference.

range.description: The line range captured at save time. For a file-scoped note this spans the whole file (1..line_count).

created.description: true when this save created a new note; false when an identical note already existed (idempotent save).

queryData.title: query --json data
queryData.description: Payload for `ynotes query --json`: every note this query returns. Anchored, drifted, and orphaned notes share one `notes` array — `status` discriminates. Orphans are always included regardless of the queried interval (the never-drop promise).

notes.description: Every note this query returns — anchored or drifted matches of the queried interval, plus every orphaned note for the file (always included). Ordered: matches first (anchored/drifted), then orphans. Group by `status` if you want the historical matched-vs-orphaned split.

malformed.description: Records for this file the index pointed at that could not be read or parsed as a note. Skipped from `notes` (they cannot be resolved) but surfaced here so a corrupt record is never silently dropped from a query (invariant #4); the remedy is `ynotes reindex`. Always present; empty array when there is nothing to flag.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories about this query — for example, that the target file does not exist (almost always a typo). The command still exits 0; the warning is the in-band signal. Always present; empty array when there is nothing to flag.

listData.title: list --json data
listData.description: Payload for `ynotes list --json`: every note in the store with its current anchor status.

malformed.description: Records the index pointed at that could not be read or parsed as a note. Skipped from `notes` (they cannot be resolved) but surfaced here so a corrupt record is never silently omitted from an inventory (invariant #4); the remedy is `ynotes reindex`. With a directory/file filter, only records under it are listed. Always present; empty array when there is nothing to flag.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories — populated when a path filter (`list <file>` or `list <dir>`) matched nothing, distinguishing 'this filter is empty' from 'the store is empty'. With no filter, an empty `notes` array is self-explanatory and `warnings` stays empty. Always present.

updateData.title: update --json data
updateData.description: Payload for `ynotes update --json`: the refreshed note's identity, plus the id it supersedes. The new note re-anchors against the current file (same target+scope, range re-resolved through the anchor ladder), so the id changes whenever the body, the file, or the resolved range did.

id.description: The refreshed note's id (content-hashed over the new identity).

previous_id.description: The id of the note this one supersedes. Equal to `id` when the update was a no-op (identical body and unchanged anchor).

range.description: The line range the refreshed bundle was captured at — the note's current resolved location.

created.description: true when this update wrote a new record; false when an identical content hash already existed.

deleteData.title: delete --json data
deleteData.description: Payload for `ynotes delete --json`. The four category arrays partition the requested ids — each requested id appears in exactly one of `deleted`, `deleted_unreadable`, `ambiguous`, `not_found`. Always emitted in full (empty arrays included) so a consumer never has to branch on key presence. Exit-code asymmetry: when `ambiguous` or `not_found` is non-empty the process exits `1` even though this remains a *success* envelope (`success: true`) — the envelope describes the partition, the exit code reports partial failure. A `deleted_unreadable` entry is a successful removal and does NOT flip the exit code. `delete` is the only command that pairs a success envelope with a non-zero exit; to detect a fully-clean delete, check that both `ambiguous` and `not_found` are empty rather than relying on the exit code or `success` alone.

requested.description: How many ids the caller passed.

deleted.description: Notes that were removed (or, under `dry_run`, would be).

body_excerpt.description: The first line of the body, truncated at 80 characters with `…`. Useful as a confirmation; not the whole body.

deleted_unreadable.description: Ids of corrupt records purged by exact id (or, under `dry_run`, that would be). A malformed record cannot be read to supply a target/scope/body, so only its id is reported. Removal requires the full 64-character id — a short prefix can never purge an unreadable record (there is no body to preview, and a prefix could otherwise catch a healthy note). An entry here is a success, not a partial failure: it does not flip the exit code.

ambiguous.description: Prefixes that matched more than one note. None of the candidates are deleted (we never silently delete multiple matches for a single requested id).

not_found.description: Prefixes that matched no note in the store.

dry_run.description: true when invoked with `--dry-run` — nothing was actually removed.

pruneData.title: prune --json data
pruneData.description: Payload for `ynotes prune --json`: orphaned notes that were removed (or, under `dry_run`, would be). Drifted notes are never touched — `reanchor` is for them.

pruned.description: One entry per orphan removed (or that would be removed).

last_known.description: The line range the orphan was anchored at the last time the resolver could locate it.

body_excerpt.description: First line of the body, truncated at 80 characters with `…`.

kept.description: How many non-orphaned notes remain in the store.

dry_run.description: true when invoked with `--dry-run` — nothing was actually removed.

reanchorData.title: reanchor --json data
reanchorData.description: Payload for `ynotes reanchor --json`. Reports every note whose selectors were refreshed in place (`changed`), every note moved to a renamed file (`relocated`), every note deliberately left untouched with the reason (`skipped`), and how many were already current (`unchanged`). Any note that moved gets a new id (the id hashes over target+bundle) — `old_id`/`new_id` carry both for lineage tracking. Under `--dry-run` the same shape is emitted with `dry_run: true` and no writes occur.

dry_run.description: true when invoked with `--dry-run` — nothing was actually written.

changed.description: Notes refreshed in place (or that would be) — the region moved or was edited within the same file. Each entry's `from` is the prior captured range; `to` is the range the refresher resolved to in the current file. A note that moved to a *different* file is reported under `relocated`, not here.

relocated.description: Notes moved to a renamed file (or that would be): git detected the target was renamed and a content rung corroborated the region at the new path. Distinct from `changed` because the note's target path changed (`from_target` -> `to_target`), so the id necessarily rotates. A rename where the region was *deleted* is not relocated — it appears in `skipped` with `reason_code: "orphaned"` (the wrong-file guard: a note is never welded onto the renamed file at an unrelated line). Always present; empty array when nothing relocated.

from_target.description: The path the note was filed under before the rename.

to_target.description: The path it now lives at (the file's current name).

from.description: Where the region sat in the old file at save time.

to.description: Where it resolved to in the renamed file.

skipped.description: Notes deliberately left untouched, with the reason. `reason_code` is the stable enum to branch on; `reason` is the human form.

reason_code.description: orphaned: no content rung located it — refreshing would weld it to guesswork. missing-target: the target file is not on disk. symlink-escape: the target resolves outside the work tree. other: a reason this contract version does not enumerate.

reason.description: Free-form human explanation suitable for display.

unchanged.description: How many notes were already current (the refreshed bundle hashed to the existing id).

reindexData.title: reindex --json data
reindexData.description: Payload for `ynotes reindex --json`. The index (`by-path.json`) is a cache rebuilt from the note records on disk, which are the source of truth; this reports how the rebuilt index differed from the one that was there. A healthy store yields empty `recovered`/`dangling`/`malformed`. Under `--dry-run` the same shape is emitted with `dry_run: true` and the on-disk index is left untouched. Reindex never invokes the anchor ladder, so note ids are unaffected.

dry_run.description: true when invoked with `--dry-run` — the on-disk index was not written.

scanned.description: Note records read successfully while walking `notes/`.

indexed.description: Distinct notes in the rebuilt index.

recovered.description: Ids found on disk that the previous index did not list — pointers that were missing and have been restored. Always present; empty when the index already agreed with disk.

dangling.description: Ids the previous index listed with no file behind them on disk — dangling pointers that have been dropped. Always present; empty when none.

malformed.description: Paths under `notes/` that could not be read or parsed as a note. Skipped (left out of the rebuilt index) but reported, never silently discarded — a readable note is never dropped and an unreadable one is never hidden. Always present; empty when none.

doctorData.title: doctor --json data
doctorData.description: Payload for `ynotes doctor --json`: the environment ynotes resolves against, plus read-only store-health diagnostics. Its `platform` and `git` values are machine-dependent, so it is not snapshot-locked.

git.description: The `git` binary's version, or null when no `git` is on PATH (the git-transport rung is then disabled).

store.description: The discovered `.ynotes` store: the string "none" when no store was found, otherwise a single-key object.

path.description: The `.ynotes` directory — present when a store was located but its notes could not be read; absent when store discovery itself failed (no valid `.ynotes` was located), in which case the implicated path is carried in `reason` instead.

reason.description: Why the store (or its notes) could not be read; carries the implicated path inline when the discrete `path` field is absent.

health.title: store health
health.description: Read-only store-health diagnostics. Present only when a store was discovered (absent when none was found). All-clean is `malformed: []`, `index.recovered: 0`, `index.dangling: 0`, `gitattributes_missing: []`.

malformed.description: Paths under `.ynotes/notes/` that could not be read or parsed as a note — present but corrupt. Surfaced so a corrupt record is visible, not silently dropped (invariant #4); the remedy is `ynotes reindex`. Always present; empty when none.

index.description: How far the by-path index cache has drifted from the notes on disk; both zero on a sound store. `ynotes reindex` reconciles it.

recovered.description: Ids present on disk but missing from the index — a reindex restores them.

dangling.description: Index pointers with no file behind them at all — a reindex drops them. A present-but-unreadable record is reported under `malformed`, not here, so one corrupt note is never double-counted.

gitattributes_missing.description: Managed `.ynotes/.gitattributes` lines absent from the store (e.g. `notes/** -merge`, `index/by-path.json merge=union`). Non-empty on a shared store means the merge guards are not in force and a future merge could corrupt note JSON; `init`/`reindex` re-add them. Always present; empty when the guards are intact.

lookupData.title: lookup --json data
lookupData.description: Payload for `ynotes lookup --json`: the notes matching a stable (target, body) handle, each with its current id and anchor status. Use this to re-derive a note's live id, which rotates on reanchor/update.

notes.description: Every note matching the lookup filters, in list order. Empty when nothing matched (exit 0).

querySpec.title: query request echo
querySpec.description: The request `query --json` echoes back: the file and location arguments exactly as passed. Shared by the full and `--count` query payloads.

file.description: The file argument as passed on the command line.

at.description: The location argument: `LINE`, `START:END`, or empty for a whole-file query.

countBreakdown.title: status breakdown
countBreakdown.description: A tally of resolved notes by anchor status, emitted by `--count` summary mode in place of the note bodies. `total` equals `anchored + drifted + orphaned`.

drifted.description: Notes located but moved or edited.

orphaned.description: Notes no content rung could locate.

queryCountData.title: query --count --json data
queryCountData.description: Payload for `ynotes query --count --json`: the status breakdown for a query in place of the note bodies, so an agent can cheaply check whether there is context here before pulling it. The resolution is identical to the full `query` (rename-following included) — only the output is condensed. Distinguished from `queryData` by carrying `count` (not `notes`); `malformed` here is a count, not an array.

malformed.description: How many records the index pointed at for this file could not be read or parsed — the count-mode analogue of `queryData.malformed[]`, so a corrupt record is still flagged in summary mode (invariant #4). Pull the full `query --json` to get their ids.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories, as in the full `query` payload. Always present; empty when there is nothing to flag.

listCountData.title: list --count --json data
listCountData.description: Payload for `ynotes list --count --json`: the status breakdown across the listed set in place of the notes. Distinguished from `listData` by carrying `count` (not `notes`); `malformed` here is a count, not an array.

malformed.description: How many records the index pointed at could not be read or parsed — the count-mode analogue of `listData.malformed[]` (invariant #4).

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories — populated when a path filter matched nothing. Always present; empty when there is nothing to flag.

showData.title: show --json data
showData.description: Payload for `ynotes show --json`: a single note selected by id (or unambiguous hex prefix), resolved against its stored target. The by-id read — `query` selects by file/line and `list` walks the store; this returns exactly one note. Resolves against the note's own `target`, so a note whose file was renamed away reads `orphaned` here; `query` on the new path is the rename-aware read.

warnings.description: Non-fatal advisories — populated, for example, when the note's target file does not exist on disk (the note then resolves `orphaned`). Always present; empty when there is nothing to flag.

note.title: Resolved note
note.description: A stored note resolved against the current file.

status.description: anchored: located and intact. drifted: located, but moved or edited. orphaned: could not be located.

stale.description: Agent convenience: false only for an anchored note; true for drifted or orphaned. A pure function of status, provided so an agent can branch on one boolean.

resolved_range.description: Where the note resolved to in the current file, or null for an orphan.

previous_range.description: Present only for a drifted or orphaned note: the range it occupied before it moved or was lost.

relocated_from.description: Present only on a `query` note surfaced under a file it was renamed *to*: the pre-rename `target` path the note is still stored under. Its presence means the note migrated here via a followed rename and a `reanchor` would make that durable; omitted for a note resolved against its own target (every `list`/`lookup` note, and any query note that matched directly).

rungs.description: Present only with --explain: each selector-ladder rung's outcome (the agreement vector).

rung.title: Rung outcome
rung.description: One selector-ladder rung's contribution to a resolution. Scores are each rung's self-assessment in [0, 100]; see the README's `--explain` section for the scoring scale.
Which rung: git transport (R1), exact quote (R2), fuzzy alignment (R3), tree-sitter structure (R4), saved position (R5).

result.description: hit: located the region. miss: ran but found nothing. skipped: could not run (e.g. not a git repo) and is not held against the result.

range.description: Present only on a hit: where this rung believes the region now is.

score.description: Present only on a hit: the rung's own confidence in its range. Scale per rung — git: 100 unchanged / 90 moved-untouched / 70 moved-touched; quote: 95 unique / 90 disambiguated by context / 55 ambiguous; structural: 55–95 (95 = identical fingerprint); fuzzy: 45–80 (capped below 90 — fuzzy alone never anchors); position: 20 in-range / 10 clamped (diagnostic only, never consulted by the verdict).

malformedNote.title: Malformed note record
malformedNote.description: A record the index points at that could not be read or parsed as a note. Surfaced by the read paths (`query`, `list`) so a corrupt record is never silently dropped and never sinks an otherwise healthy read (invariant #4). The remedy is `ynotes reindex`. Note: such a record cannot be selected by `delete`/`update` (it cannot be read to match) — reindex or a manual fix is the path.

id.description: The id the index filed this record under — its on-disk filename stem. The corruption is in the record's contents, not its name, so the id is still well-formed.

error.description: Why the record could not be read or parsed. Free-form, for display — branch on an entry being present, not on this text.

noteId.description: Content-addressed note id: the SHA-256, hex-encoded, of (target, scope, anchor, body). Deterministic — no timestamp or randomness. **Rotates on reanchor and update**: refreshing the anchor or replacing the body changes the hash inputs and so changes the id. To cache a stable handle to a note across reanchors, use the (target, scope, body) tuple rather than the id; `created_at` is preserved across reanchor and is exposed by `list --json` in a future schema version.

target.description: The note's target file, relative to the store's work tree, with forward slashes.

scope.description: What the note is attached to: a contiguous line range, or the whole file. A single-line note is `range` with `range[0] == range[1]`. (v3 collapsed the v2 `line` variant into `range` so consumers handle one representation; the internal note-id hash still distinguishes intent so existing ids stay valid.)

schemaVersion.description: The contract version. Bumped on any field change; consumers should reject an unrecognised value. v11 added two read surfaces: the `show` subcommand (`showData` — one note by id/prefix, resolved against its stored target) and a `--count` summary mode on `query` and `list` (`queryCountData` / `listCountData` — a status breakdown in place of the note bodies, so an agent can cheaply check for context before pulling it). Both are additive; `list --explain` also gained the optional `rungs` field that `query --explain` already emitted, with no shape change. v10 followed file renames: `reanchor` gained an always-present `relocated[]` array (notes moved to a renamed file, corroborated at the new path), and the shared resolved-`note` object gained an optional `relocated_from` (present only on a `query` note surfaced under a file it was renamed to — the pre-rename path it is still stored under); no existing payload field changed. v9 added an always-present `deleted_unreadable[]` array to `delete` (ids of *corrupt* records purged by exact id — they cannot be read to supply a target/scope/body, so they are listed as bare ids rather than rich `deleted[]` entries; an entry here is a success, not a failure, and does not flip the exit code); no existing payload field changed. v8 added an always-present `malformed[]` array to `query` and `list` (records the index points at that cannot be read or parsed — surfaced rather than dropped or made fatal, invariant #4) and a `health` object to `doctor` (store-health diagnostics: malformed records, index drift, missing managed `.gitattributes` lines); no existing payload field changed. v7 added the `lookupData` payload for the new `lookup` subcommand (resolve a stable (target, body) handle to live note ids); no existing payload changed. v6 added the `reindexData` payload for the new `reindex` subcommand (rebuild the by-path index from disk); no existing payload changed. v5 unified `query`'s `matched`/`orphaned` arrays into a single `notes` array (status discriminates), aligning query with `list`, and added payloads for the new `update`, `delete`, and `prune` subcommands. v4 wrapped every payload in a `{success, v, data | error+type}` envelope and emits that envelope on stdout regardless of exit code. v3 added the always-present `warnings` array and collapsed the `line` scope into `range`.
